title: Brand-specific elevation & blur harmonization for translucent panels in deep-dark console
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Several brand integrations display inconsistent color and perceived depth when rendered on translucent panels in our deep-dark console theme. On translucent surfaces with backdrop-blur and micro-elevation, brand accents (especially saturated primarys) appear to 'bleed' or shift hue, causing contrast regressions in charts, table headers, and CTA buttons.

Goal: Create a concise set of token rules and component overrides to harmonize elevation, blur, and brand tinting for translucent panels in deep-dark surfaces so that: 1) text and interactive controls meet WCAG contrast targets; 2) brand accents remain identifiable but not oversaturated; 3) components maintain consistent perceived depth across regions and brand themes.

Scope: token mapping changes, alpha composition rules, component overrides for Panel/Card, Table headers, Primary/Secondary buttons, and Chart area fills. This ticket drives the design spec and acceptance criteria; implementation tickets will be created for tokens and code changes in the component library and console CSS variables.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec defines 3 micro-elevation steps for translucent panels with explicit alpha values (overlay alpha, tint alpha, blur radius) per step
Token mappings for brand-anchored accents include a saturation clamp and perceptual lightness adjustment for deep-dark surfaces
All examples (tables, charts, buttons, cards) pass contrast checks: text >= 4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for secondary labels where applicable
Figma file updated with component variants for at least 4 customer brand colors showing before/after
Developer token export (json) compatible with console-2026.03 theming pipeline and a reference PR linked
design_notes:
Proposal highlights: 1) Introduce 'anchor-neutral' token that is a neutralized blend of brand primary and deep-dark background; used for strokes and subtle tints. 2) Apply a saturation clamp (reduce S by 20-40%) when brand primary is applied to translucent surfaces to avoid color bleed. 3) Add an alpha-composite matrix: for each micro-elevation step (E0, E1, E2) specify overlayAlpha, tintAlpha, blurPx. 4) For charts, use an 'accent-outline' token for line strokes to preserve readability while reducing fill vibrance. 5) Buttons: primary-filled on translucent panels should use elevated-surface-primary (tone-shifted) with a soft border to preserve affordance.

Accessibility trade-offs: We preserve brand recognizability while prioritizing text contrast. For very low-contrast brand palettes, fallback to a neutralized accent is required. We prefer subtle motion (press depth) to communicate elevation rather than larger color saturation changes.

Implementation notes for engineers: Provide a small, deterministic color transform algorithm (HSL-based with L and S clamps) that runs during token compile, plus token flags so runtime can pick 'translucent-aware' tokens per surface. Avoid runtime heavy operations; apply transforms at build/compile time where possible.
tasks: Audit current components with translucent backgrounds across console pages (dashboard, model detail, billing) - assigned to Kunal
Create alpha-composite matrix and token naming convention (design token + surface suffix) - Ava to author spec
Update Figma components with new variants and document contrast proofs
Prototype small CSS variables export and share with infra for token pipeline compatibility
Open implementation PR in components repo with token JSON and example stories
Run cross-brand QA with 4 customer brand swatches and log regressions
decisions: Use perceptual lightness adjustments over radial gradients for depth cues to reduce GPU cost
Clamp brand saturation when applied to translucent panels rather than dimming hue by default
Provide explicit developer tokens for 'elevated-surface-primary' rather than requiring runtime blends
